categoryName: First aid and medical devices — thermometer, BP monitor, glucometer + strips, oximeter, nebuliser, hot/cold packs, crepe bandage, wheelchair/crutches

skuLines.line: Digital clinical thermometer — underarm/oral, flexible tip
skuLines.examples: Dr Morepen MT-100/MT-222, Dr Trust 605, Omron MC-246, AccuSure MT-1027
skuLines.packSizes: single unit, blister/box; 10-unit inner for institutional buy
skuLines.seasonality: Sep-Oct and Mar-Apr season-change fever waves; Dec-Feb hill winter
skuLines.notes: Notified medical device — retail sale of notified devices needs a sale licence (Form MD-42) from the state licensing authority; confirm with the HP Drug Controller. Ships flat, no cold chain. ALWAYS stock the LR41/LR44 button cell beside it — a dead cell makes the unit look defective and there is no replacement within 30 km.

skuLines.examples: Dr Trust 601, Omron MC-720, Beurer FT 90, HealthSense Accu-Scan FT 500
skuLines.seasonality: Nov-Feb; term-start (Apr, Jul) when hostels screen new arrivals
skuLines.notes: The hostel/infirmary and canteen screening buy — sell 1-2 institutional units per wing, not just retail. Needs AAA cells stocked alongside. Notified device (MD-42). Accuracy drifts in cold ambient air; a hill winter morning reading runs low, so keep a digital contact thermometer as the confirm.

skuLines.examples: Hicks clinical thermometer, Dr Odin glass thermometer, spirit-filled (mercury-free) prismatic
skuLines.seasonality: year-round, winter skew
skuLines.notes: Older staff and grandparents still ask for the glass one and distrust digital. Stock ONLY spirit-filled / mercury-free — mercury-added thermometers are being phased out under the Minamata Convention and MoHFW mercury-free-healthcare advisories (verify current status before ordering). Breakage in transit is high on hill roads: order in padded cartons and expect 3-5% shrink.

skuLines.line: Automatic upper-arm BP monitor — entry level
skuLines.examples: Dr Morepen BP-02/BP-15, Dr Trust 129, Omron HEM-7121J, AccuSure TD-3128
skuLines.packSizes: single unit with 22-32cm cuff, adaptor or 4x AA
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; spikes after campus health camps and Nov-Jan (cold raises readings, more people check)
skuLines.notes: The single highest-consequence device line here: hypertensive teaching staff and elderly residents cannot drive 50 km to get a reading. Notified device (MD-42). Keep a working demo unit on the counter — nobody buys a ₹2,000 device unattended. Warranty service is off-campus, so prefer brands with courier-based service (Omron, Dr Morepen) and keep the box + bill. Stock spare 22-32cm cuffs and the mains adaptor separately; cuffs perish and are the usual failure.

skuLines.line: Automatic upper-arm BP monitor — premium / app-connected
skuLines.examples: Omron HEM-7156T, Omron HEM-7361T (AFib), Beurer BM 54, Dr Trust 123 Bluetooth
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; gifting spike Diwali and at retirement/farewell
skuLines.notes: One or two facings only — senior faculty, doctors at the campus hospital, and children buying for a parent. Bluetooth/app models are becoming the default at this price point in India. Low turn, high ticket: order-in rather than deep stock, and never hold more than 2 pieces (firmware/model refresh makes old stock unsellable).

skuLines.examples: Omron HEM-6161, Dr Trust 205, Beurer BC 21
skuLines.seasonality: year-round
skuLines.notes: Only for people who genuinely cannot manage an arm cuff (obesity, arm injury, travel). Clinically less reliable than upper-arm — counsel, don't upsell. Keep one facing.

skuLines.examples: Diamond BPAN 01/Deluxe aneroid, Rossmax GB102, Niscomed aneroid; MCP/Microtone stethoscope, 3M Littmann Classic III
skuLines.packSizes: single set; aneroid + stethoscope sold together or separately
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; institutional order at academic-year start
skuLines.notes: Institutional line, not a consumer one: the school infirmary, university health centre and campus hospital nursing staff. Sell as a set with a spare bulb and valve. Aneroid gauges drift and need recalibration every 1-2 years — offer to send the batch out with a service run.

skuLines.examples: Accu-Chek Active, OneTouch Select Plus Simple, Dr Morepen Gluco One BG-03, AccuSure Simple
skuLines.packSizes: single kit with carry case, 10 strips, 10 lancets, lancing device
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; spikes right after any campus diabetes screening camp
skuLines.marginBand: 10-20% (razor — sold thin, sometimes at cost, to lock the strip annuity)
skuLines.notes: The meter is the razor, the strips are the blade — this is the most valuable annuity line in the whole category. Choose ONE or at most TWO strip ecosystems for the store and stand by them; every extra meter brand strands a strip SKU in dead stock. Notified device/IVD (MD-42). Never sell a meter without confirming you will hold its strips for the next 3 years.

skuLines.examples: Accu-Chek Active 50s, OneTouch Select Plus 50s, Dr Morepen BG-03 strips 50s, AccuSure 50s (Dr Trust 9003 50s live at ₹749 vs ₹938 MRP)
skuLines.seasonality: year-round, flat and predictable — the most forecastable line in the category
skuLines.marginBand: 15-25% MNC, 25-35% Indian brands (4-box packs discount to ~20%)
skuLines.notes: HILL-LOGISTICS TRAP: strips are humidity- and temperature-sensitive (store 4-30°C, dry) and expire 18-24 months unopened but only 3-6 months after the vial is opened. Baru Sahib's heavy monsoon humidity is a real risk — store in the dry, sealed, off the floor. Order by name-list, not by hunch: identify the ~30-60 known diabetics on campus, hold 6-8 weeks of THEIR brand, and no more. A stock-out here forces a 100 km round trip; over-stock here expires and is a write-off.

skuLines.examples: Accu-Chek Softclix lancets 100s, OneTouch Delica 25s/100s, Dr Morepen lancets 25s, universal 28G lancets
skuLines.packSizes: 25, 50, 100 per box; lancing device sold single
skuLines.seasonality: year-round
skuLines.notes: Lancets are brand-locked to the lancing device — match them to whatever meters you sell. High-margin, tiny, never expires meaningfully: the easiest line to keep 3 months deep. Sell a sharps disposal tin alongside; loose used lancets in a hostel dustbin is a real injury risk.

skuLines.examples: Dr Trust 210/Signature, BPL Smart Oxy, Beurer PO 30, Control D, Choicemmed
skuLines.seasonality: Nov-Feb respiratory season; any flu outbreak in the hostels
skuLines.notes: Post-COVID this is now a normal household device and the replacement cycle (units bought 2020-21 are dying) drives steady sales. Critical here because the nearest hospital escalation is a hill drive: a low SpO2 reading is what triggers a family to move. Notified device (MD-42). Cheap Chinese units under ₹500 read badly on cold fingers — a genuine problem in a Himachal winter; stock a mid-tier brand and say why.

skuLines.examples: Dr Trust ES-01, HealthSense Ultra-Lite PS 126, Omron HN-289, Equinox EQ-EB-6172
skuLines.packSizes: single unit, glass/plastic platform, CR2032 or 2x AAA
skuLines.seasonality: Jan (resolutions), Apr-Jun (sports/fitness), term start
skuLines.notes: Broad-appeal, easy sell to students and staff alike. Bulky-ish but light and stackable — good use of shelf. Glass platforms crack in transit on hill roads; insist on double-boxed cartons. Stock CR2032 cells beside it.

skuLines.examples: Beurer BY 80, Dr Trust digital baby scale, Equinox baby scale, Bonsaii tray scale
skuLines.seasonality: year-round
skuLines.notes: Married staff quarters with newborns is a real cohort here, and there is no paediatric clinic to weigh at weekly. Very low turn (maybe 6-15 units a year across 5,000 residents) — hold ONE, and consider offering weighing free at the counter instead of selling the device (see adjacent services).

skuLines.examples: Prega News, i-can, Velocit, Clearblue
skuLines.seasonality: year-round
skuLines.notes: Legitimate and steady demand from married staff families, and there is nowhere else within 30-50 km to buy one. Handle with discretion: keep behind the counter or in an opaque bag rather than on an open peg in a small township where everyone knows everyone — the alternative is the sale simply does not happen. IVD, licence applies. 24-month shelf life, watch expiry on a slow-moving line.

skuLines.examples: Omron NE-C101 / NE-C28, Dr Morepen CN-01/CN-06, Nulife Mist (Medtech Life), Philips InnoSpire Essence
skuLines.packSizes: single unit with adult mask, child mask, mouthpiece, tubing, medicine cup
skuLines.seasonality: Strong Oct-Feb peak (hill winter, wheezing, bronchiolitis in small children); second bump in the monsoon
skuLines.notes: For a cold-hill campus with a residential school full of children, this is a genuine must-have and probably under-appreciated. A child wheezing at 2am with the nearest chemist 30 km away is exactly the case ARY exists to cover. Notified device (MD-42). Mains-powered — check it survives the local voltage; recommend a unit with a 1-year warranty and a serviceable pump. Stock 3-4 pieces before winter, not in January when they sell out.

skuLines.line: Nebuliser mask / tube / medicine-cup replacement kit
skuLines.examples: Omron adult & child nebuliser kit, Dr Morepen neb kit, Nulife mask set, generic paediatric mask + 2m tubing
skuLines.packSizes: single kit (mask + tube + cup); mask alone; tubing alone
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Feb with the nebuliser season
skuLines.notes: The forgotten consumable that turns a device sale into repeat revenue. Masks and tubing harden, crack and go mouldy — a family with an asthmatic child buys 2-3 sets a year. Paediatric masks sell faster than adult here. Match to the nebuliser brands on your shelf; universal 22mm fittings cover most.

skuLines.line: Electric steam inhaler / vaporiser + inhalant capsules
skuLines.examples: Vicks Steam Inhaler V-1300, Dr Morepen vaporizer, Dr Trust 706 steam vaporizer; Karvol Plus capsules, Vicks inhalant
skuLines.packSizes: device single; capsules 10s; inhalant sticks single
skuLines.seasonality: Very sharp Oct-Feb peak — this is a hill-winter hero SKU
skuLines.notes: Cheap, high-turn, and unglamorous — the volume winner of the respiratory shelf in a cold location. Build a winter end-cap: vaporiser + capsules + chest rub + hot water bag together. Devices are light and cube cheaply; over-order rather than under-order for November.

skuLines.line: Asthma support — inhaler spacer / holding chamber and peak flow meter
skuLines.examples: Cipla Zerostat VT spacer, Lupin Babyhaler, Cipla Peak Flow Meter, Omron PFM 20
skuLines.packSizes: single unit; spacer with paediatric or adult mask
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Feb; Mar-Apr pollen
skuLines.notes: A residential school of 5-18 year olds will have a meaningful number of diagnosed asthmatics whose spacers get lost, crushed or outgrown mid-term, and the parents are not on campus. Hold 2-3 paediatric spacers permanently. Coordinate with the school infirmary so they can point parents at you instead of a town trip.

skuLines.line: Adhesive bandages (band-aids) — plain, washproof, and kids' printed
skuLines.examples: Band-Aid Washproof 10s/20s, Band-Aid cartoon/Marvel strips, Dettol Plaster, Handyplast
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; peaks with the school sports/athletics meet and monsoon (wet stone paths, slips)
skuLines.notes: The single highest-unit-velocity SKU in this entire category for a school campus. Stock the cartoon/printed variants for the junior school — they outsell plain strips to children by a wide margin and carry better margin. Also sell 100s tins to hostel wardens and the two canteens as an institutional line. Keep it at the counter, not deep in an aisle: it is an impulse and an emergency buy at once.

skuLines.examples: Dettol Antiseptic Liquid 100/250/550ml, Savlon Antiseptic Liquid, Suthol
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon Jul-Sep peak (wound infection risk); year-round base
skuLines.notes: Household staple AND institutional buy — hostels, canteens and the warehouse all take 1L packs. Thin margin on Dettol, so push the 1L/5L institutional SKU where margin is better and freight per litre is lower. Flammable-ish liquid in bulk: check storage.

skuLines.line: Antiseptic and antibiotic skin cream / ointment
skuLines.examples: Savlon Antiseptic Cream 20g, Betadine ointment 15g, Soframycin Skin Cream 30g, Neosporin powder
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon Jul-Sep; year-round base
skuLines.notes: Several of these are drugs, not devices — Soframycin and Betadine ointment need a retail DRUG licence (Form 20/21), which is a different licence from the medical-device MD-42. Confirm which licences ARY actually holds before shelving these; if it holds neither, the honest answer is that the campus hospital pharmacy covers them and ARY sticks to devices and dressings. Small tubes, 24-36 month shelf life, easy to hold.

skuLines.examples: Cipladine / Betadine 5% solution 100ml, surgical spirit 100ml, hydrogen peroxide 6%, Romsons alcohol swabs 100s, Sterillium
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon and sports season
skuLines.notes: Spirit and peroxide are cheap, fast-moving and almost pure margin, and the infirmary buys them by the case. Spirit is a flammable liquid — store away from the heating aisle and do not stack near the hot-water-bag/heating-pad display. Note the institutional sensitivity: surgical spirit is a medical antiseptic, not a beverage, but keep it behind the counter in a dry-campus institution to avoid any misreading.

skuLines.examples: Bella / Sri absorbent cotton 25g/50g/100g, Ginni Filaments cotton roll 500g, Datt Mediproducts, JOJO
skuLines.seasonality: year-round
skuLines.notes: Bulky and light — freight per rupee of value is poor on a hill road, so buy 500g institutional rolls and, if permitted, let the infirmary and canteens take those directly. Humidity is the enemy: cotton absorbs monsoon moisture, discolours and loses its 'sterile-looking' appeal, which kills sales. Keep sealed, on a pallet or shelf, never on a stone floor.

skuLines.examples: Datt Sterile Gauze Swab 5x5cm / 7.5x7.5cm, Romsons gauze pads, Dyna, Medisilk
skuLines.seasonality: Monsoon and sports season
skuLines.notes: The infirmary/hospital is the volume buyer; households buy 5s and 10s. Sterile packs have a real expiry (3-5 years) and the sterile barrier fails if the pouch is crushed or damp — rotate FIFO and reject damp cartons on receipt. Stock both the household small pack and the 100s institutional box.

skuLines.examples: Datt roller gauze bandage, Romsons roll bandage, unbleached mill bandage cloth
skuLines.seasonality: year-round
skuLines.notes: Cheapest wound-securing option and what a hostel matron actually reaches for. Buy by the 12-roll inner. Non-sterile variants are fine for over-dressing and much cheaper — carry both and know which is which.

skuLines.examples: Tynor Elastic Crepe Bandage 6/8/10/15cm, Dyna Crepe, Vissco crepe bandage, Flamingo crepe
skuLines.packSizes: single roll (4m stretched); 10cm is the volume size
skuLines.seasonality: Sharp peaks at the annual sports/athletics meet, inter-house tournaments, and monsoon (slips on wet stone)
skuLines.notes: With ~2,000+ school and university students playing sport on hill ground, sprains are the highest-frequency injury on this campus and the crepe bandage is the standard answer. Carry all four widths — 10cm for knees/ankles, 6cm for wrists/children. Reusable, so repeat rate is lower than band-aids but the ticket is 3-5x. Pair on-shelf with the instant cold pack and the knee cap: one injury, three SKUs.

skuLines.line: Adhesive tape — micropore and zinc oxide plaster
skuLines.examples: 3M Micropore 1"/2", Leukoplast, Dynaplast zinc oxide plaster, Romsons Surgi-Tape
skuLines.packSizes: 1" and 2" x 5m/9m rolls; single and 6/12-roll inner
skuLines.seasonality: year-round
skuLines.notes: Nobody buys tape on its own — it sells as the third item beside gauze and cotton, so merchandise the three together. Adhesive dries out in stored heat and fails; 2-3 year shelf life, rotate. The infirmary takes 12-roll inners.

skuLines.examples: Burnol 20g, Silverex Ionic gel, hydrogel burn dressing (Dermafill/Medline), sterile non-adherent pad
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes around Diwali/Lohri and any festival cooking
skuLines.notes: Under-stocked almost everywhere and specifically wrong to under-stock HERE: ARY serves TWO canteens plus a warehouse plus 5,000 residents cooking in staff quarters. Scald and oil burns are the predictable industrial injury of a campus kitchen. Sell a dedicated kitchen burn kit to each canteen (burn gel + non-adherent pads + cling film + cold pack) and restock it quarterly. Burnol is a drug — licence caveat applies.

skuLines.examples: 3M Tegaderm, Handyplast Aqua, Dynaplast Waterproof, Medipore
skuLines.seasonality: Heavy monsoon Jul-Sep — the reason this line exists here
skuLines.notes: A hill monsoon means a dressing gets soaked walking between blocks and a soaked dressing is an infected wound. This is the one 'premium' dressing worth explaining at the counter. Long shelf life, tiny cube, sterile barrier must stay intact.

skuLines.line: Assembled first aid kit — home, vehicle, and wall-mounted
skuLines.examples: St John Ambulance first aid kit, Kudize home kit, Prime Safety wall-mount metal box, Dr Trust first aid kit; own-assembled ARY kit
skuLines.packSizes: pouch (10-25 items), box (40-90 items), wall-mount cabinet
skuLines.seasonality: Term start (Apr and Jul) when parents kit out a hosteller; new-staff-quarters allocation
skuLines.notes: The best margin play in the category: assemble ARY's own kit from lines already on the shelf and price it as a bundle — you capture the margin on 12 SKUs in one ₹500 sale. Three distinct buyers: parents kitting a hosteller, staff for the quarters, and the institution for wall-mounting in every hostel wing, canteen, lab, workshop and school bus (buses legally need a first aid box). Sell the institutional version WITH a quarterly restock-and-check-expiry service.

skuLines.line: Barrier protection — disposable gloves and face masks
skuLines.examples: Romsons / Kimberly-Clark nitrile gloves 100s, Dr Trust latex gloves, Venus / Magnum 3-ply masks 50s, Venus V-4400 N95
skuLines.seasonality: Nov-Feb flu season; any outbreak in the hostels
skuLines.notes: Now a normal, boring, steady line rather than a panic one — infirmary, canteens (food handling), warehouse and cleaning staff are the reliable buyers. Latex is cheaper but allergenic; carry nitrile for the kitchens. Masks have a 3-year shelf life and were massively over-bought industry-wide, so buy shallow at good prices. Do not build a COVID-sized stack.

skuLines.line: First aid instruments and CPR barrier
skuLines.examples: stainless first aid scissors, splinter tweezers, safety pins card, Romsons CPR pocket mask / face shield, LED penlight
skuLines.packSizes: single instruments; blister card of safety pins
skuLines.priceBand: Scissors ₹80-300; tweezers ₹40-150; safety pins ₹20-50; CPR shield ₹150-600; penlight ₹100-400
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; institutional at academic-year start
skuLines.notes: Low turn individually, but these are what make an assembled kit credible, so most units move inside a bundle rather than alone. The CPR face shield is an institutional/first-responder line — sell to the infirmary and to whoever runs the school's first aid training, not off an open peg. Splinter tweezers genuinely sell on a wooded hill campus.

skuLines.line: Sterile eye wash, saline and eye pads
skuLines.examples: sterile normal saline 0.9% 100ml (Nirlife/Otsuka), sterile eye pad (Datt), plastic eye wash cup
skuLines.seasonality: Mar-Jun dust and pollen; conjunctivitis outbreaks spread fast in hostels
skuLines.notes: Conjunctivitis in a residential school is an outbreak, not a case — when it hits, saline, eye pads and separate towels sell out in days. Keep a modest permanent stock and know your reorder lead time. Sterile saline is also the correct first-line wound irrigation, so it double-duties with the wound-care shelf.

skuLines.examples: Electral 21.8g sachet, Enerzal, Prolyte, ORSL ready-to-drink, zinc dispersible tablets
skuLines.seasonality: Apr-Jun heat and Jul-Sep monsoon GI illness; any hostel-wide stomach upset
skuLines.notes: Cheap, tiny, 2-3 year shelf life, and the one item where a stock-out is genuinely dangerous in a place 30-50 km from a hospital — a hostel-wide gastro episode can need 200 sachets in 48 hours. Hold a deliberate buffer of 300-500 sachets going into monsoon and make sure the infirmary knows you have it. WHO-formula ORS is a drug (licence caveat); the RTD drinks are not.

skuLines.examples: Kudos instant cold pack, Sportsoul instant ice pack, Romsons cold pack
skuLines.seasonality: Sports meet, inter-house tournaments, PT/games periods — Aug-Feb on a school calendar
skuLines.notes: One-shot chemistry pack — no freezer needed, which matters where a hostel wing has no reliable fridge. The natural bundle partner for the crepe bandage. Sell 12s boxes to the games department and the infirmary bench. 2-3 year shelf life, light, cubes well.

skuLines.examples: Tynor Hot & Cold Pack, Vissco gel pack, Dr Trust gel pack, Flamingo reusable pack
skuLines.seasonality: Cold use in the sports season; hot use Oct-Feb for joint pain
skuLines.notes: Dual-season, which is rare and valuable — cold for sprains in summer/autumn, hot for arthritic knees through a Himachal winter. Reusable so no repeat, but the ticket is decent and it sells alongside every sprain. Gel packs split with age and freeze-thaw cycles; do not hold stock more than a year.

skuLines.line: Hot water bag — rubber and electric
skuLines.examples: Duckback / Flamingo rubber hot water bag, Tynor hot water bottle, Dr Trust electric hot water bag, Ozomax
skuLines.packSizes: 1.5L, 2L rubber bags with or without cover; electric bag single
skuLines.seasonality: Very sharp Oct-Feb — with the steam vaporiser, the defining winter SKU of a cold hill location
skuLines.notes: Probably the single highest-volume seasonal item in this whole category for Baru Sahib: everybody from a 6-year-old hosteller to an 80-year-old wants one in December, and there is nowhere else to buy it. IMPORTANT PERISHABILITY: rubber bags degrade, crack and burst-scald if held in stock across years — buy FRESH each September, sell through by February, do not carry leftovers to the next winter. Electric bags need a safety-marked unit; cheap ones are a burn risk. Order the season's quantity in Aug-Sep, before hill freight tightens.

skuLines.examples: Dr Trust 387 Electric Heating Pad (live ₹1,299 vs ₹1,499), Flamingo electric heating pad, Vissco heating belt, Beurer HK 35
skuLines.packSizes: single unit, small/large pad, orthopaedic belt form
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Feb
skuLines.notes: The upgrade sale from the hot water bag — for back and knee pain in older staff and for period pain. Mains-powered: confirm it tolerates local voltage swings and carries a proper safety mark, and keep the warranty box. Hold 3-6 units for the winter, not deep stock; unsold units carry cleanly to next winter (unlike rubber bags), so the risk is low.

skuLines.examples: Tynor Knee Cap J-01 / Knee Support D-08, Vissco knee cap, Flamingo knee support, LP Support
skuLines.packSizes: S / M / L / XL / XXL — sizing is the whole game
skuLines.seasonality: Sports season for the young; Oct-Feb for arthritic knees in the cold
skuLines.notes: Two totally different buyers with the same SKU: a 19-year-old footballer and a 65-year-old with osteoarthritis climbing campus steps. Steep terrain makes knees the dominant complaint of a hill township. STOCK ALL SIZES — a knee cap in the wrong size is a returned sale and a lost customer, and size-run gaps are the classic ortho-support failure. Keep a measuring tape at the counter.

skuLines.line: Joint and limb supports — ankle binder, wrist splint, elbow support, finger splint
skuLines.examples: Tynor Ankle Binder D-01, Tynor Wrist Splint E-01/E-03, Tynor Elbow Support, Tynor Finger Extension Splint, Vissco equivalents
skuLines.packSizes: S/M/L/XL each; left/right for some wrist splints
skuLines.seasonality: Sports season Aug-Feb; monsoon slips Jul-Sep
skuLines.notes: Sprained ankles and jammed fingers are the everyday output of a school playground on hill ground, and each of these is a same-day need. Carry a shallow but COMPLETE grid — every type in M and L at minimum — rather than deep stock of one. Wrist splints often come left/right specific: check before ordering.

skuLines.examples: Tynor Cervical Collar Soft B-01 / B-02 (with chin support), Vissco soft collar, Flamingo cervical collar
skuLines.packSizes: S / M / L; with and without chin support
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; winter neck stiffness
skuLines.notes: Prescribed after a whiplash, a hill-road accident, or for cervical spondylosis in desk-bound faculty — and it is prescribed at the hospital, then needed the same hour. Carry M and L permanently. This is exactly the 'you only need it once, but you need it NOW, and town is 50 km away' item that justifies ARY holding slow stock.

skuLines.examples: Tynor LS Belt A-01 / Contoured LS Belt A-04, Vissco lumbar sacral belt, Flamingo LS belt
skuLines.packSizes: S / M / L / XL / XXL by waist size
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; spikes with warehouse loading work and Oct-Feb
skuLines.notes: Real, specific demand here: warehouse and canteen staff lifting sacks, drivers on hill roads, and teachers with chronic low-back pain. Waist-size run matters as much as with knee caps. Good ticket, good margin, no expiry — one of the safest slow-moving lines to hold.

skuLines.examples: Tynor Pouch Arm Sling C-01, Tynor Universal Sling, Vissco arm sling, Flamingo shoulder immobiliser
skuLines.packSizes: S / M / L; child sizes for the school
skuLines.seasonality: Sports season; monsoon falls
skuLines.notes: A fractured or dislocated arm in a residential school is a near-certainty several times a year, and the sling is needed on the way back from the hospital. STOCK CHILD SIZES — this is the sizing gap most stores miss, and a school of 5-18 year olds is exactly where it bites. Two adult and two child pieces permanently.

skuLines.examples: Tynor Abdominal Support Belt A-06, Vissco abdominal binder, Flamingo post-pregnancy belt
skuLines.seasonality: year-round
skuLines.notes: Married staff quarters means post-caesarean and post-abdominal-surgery recovery happens on campus, with nowhere nearby to buy the belt the surgeon told them to wear. Discreet handling and a female staff member to advise on sizing will make or break this line. Also used post-hernia-repair by older men.

skuLines.examples: Comprezon (Vissco) varicose vein stockings, Tynor medical compression stockings, Sigvaris
skuLines.packSizes: Class 1 / Class 2; knee-length and thigh-length; S/M/L/XL
skuLines.seasonality: year-round
skuLines.notes: Teachers stand all day on hard floors and hill paths — varicose veins are an occupational reality for the faculty. Prescribed by class and measured by calf circumference, so this needs a competent fitting or the pair is wrong and returned. Hold one or two and order the rest to measurement rather than stocking a size grid.

skuLines.line: Walking stick — single-point, L-shape, tripod and quadripod
skuLines.examples: Vissco walking stick, Tynor Walking Stick L-13, Karma tripod stick, Flamingo quadripod stick
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; Oct-Feb (ice, wet stone, poor light)
skuLines.notes: On a steep campus with stone paths, a stick is mobility, not an accessory, and the elderly cohort is the one that literally cannot make the trip to town to buy one. Cheap, light, hangs on a wall hook, no expiry — the easiest of all the mobility aids to justify stocking. Sell with a replacement rubber ferrule (the tip wears out on stone and is the reason sticks slip).

skuLines.examples: Tynor Auxiliary Crutches, Tynor Elbow Crutches, Vissco crutches, Karma elbow crutches, Flamingo underarm crutches
skuLines.packSizes: sold as a PAIR; adult and child heights; adjustable
skuLines.seasonality: Sports season and monsoon
skuLines.notes: Every fractured ankle on this campus needs crutches within hours of the plaster going on, and the family is not driving 100 km for them. Hold ONE adult pair and ONE child/short pair, and rent rather than sell (see adjacent services) — a crutch is needed for six weeks, then stored forever, so rental both serves the resident better and turns the same asset over 6-8 times a year. Bulky: order in the same consignment as wheelchairs to share freight.

skuLines.examples: Vissco folding walker, Karma walking frame, Tynor walker, Flamingo rollator with wheels and brakes
skuLines.packSizes: single, folding, height-adjustable; with or without front wheels
skuLines.seasonality: year-round
skuLines.notes: Post-surgery and post-fracture rehabilitation, and frail elderly residents. Bulky, low turn, high consequence — classic rental candidate, not a sale item. Stock one folding walker; order rollators only against a named request. Freight and storage are the real cost, not the purchase price.

skuLines.examples: Karma KM-2500, Vissco Comfort / Champion wheelchair, Med-E-Move folding wheelchair, Insta wheelchair
skuLines.packSizes: single, folding, fixed or detachable arm/footrest; 16"/18" seat
skuLines.seasonality: year-round
skuLines.notes: The most-discussed and most-mis-stocked line in this category. Buying one to SELL ties up ₹8,000 in stock that may move twice a year. The right answer for a closed township is ONE or TWO units held for RENTAL at a deposit — a broken hip, a post-operative resident, a visiting elderly parent, a school prize-day guest. That converts dead stock into recurring revenue and is the service residents cannot get anywhere within 50 km. Bulky freight (charge it into the rental), and campus terrain is steep: an attendant-push model with good brakes beats a self-propel here.

skuLines.line: Bed-care items — commode chair, bedpan, urinal pot, anti-bedsore air mattress
skuLines.examples: Vissco / Karma commode chair, stainless and plastic bedpan, Romsons male urinal pot, Apex / Med-E-Move anti-bedsore air mattress with pump
skuLines.packSizes: single each; mattress with electric pump
skuLines.seasonality: year-round
skuLines.notes: For bed-bound elderly residents and post-operative recovery in staff quarters. Bedpans and urinals are cheap and worth stocking (they are also bought by the campus hospital). Commode chairs and air mattresses are rental-only in a store this size — nobody wants to own one after the recovery, and holding them as stock is money on a shelf. Air mattress pumps are mains-powered and fail; keep the warranty.

skuLines.examples: 7-day AM-PM pill organiser (Dr Trust / Kudize), 4-compartment daily box, pill cutter
skuLines.seasonality: year-round
skuLines.notes: Tiny, cheap, no expiry, high margin, and genuinely useful to elderly residents on 5-8 daily medicines with no pharmacist to ask. Sells best displayed at the BP-monitor and strip shelf, not on its own. A pill cutter beside it is an easy add-on.

skuLines.line: Infant dosing aids — oral syringe, dropper, measuring cup
skuLines.examples: Farlin / Chicco medicine dropper, Romsons oral dosing syringe, Pigeon medicine feeder, graduated measuring cup
skuLines.seasonality: Nov-Feb illness season
skuLines.notes: Married staff with infants have nowhere to buy a 2ml oral syringe at 9pm, and dosing a baby by kitchen spoon is how overdoses happen. Cheap, tiny, high margin. Merchandise on the baby-care shelf as well as here — dual placement doubles the sell-through on a line this small.

skuLines.line: Baby nasal care — aspirator and saline drops
skuLines.examples: Pigeon / Farlin nasal aspirator, bulb syringe, Nasoclear saline drops, Nasivion Saline, Otrivin Saline
skuLines.seasonality: Sharp Oct-Feb peak — a blocked-nose baby in a cold hill winter is the classic 2am emergency
skuLines.notes: Under-appreciated must-have for THIS population specifically: babies in unheated hill quarters through a Himachal winter, with the nearest chemist 30 km down a mountain road. Cheap to stock, sells with the nebuliser and vaporiser. Saline drops are a device-adjacent product with a short 2-3 month in-use life once opened — customers buy repeatedly.

skuLines.examples: Dettol Instant Hand Sanitizer 50/200/500ml, Savlon Hexa, Lifebuoy, Sterillium
skuLines.seasonality: Nov-Feb flu season; any outbreak
skuLines.notes: Now a boring commodity — buy shallow, sell the 5L institutional pack to canteens, hostels and the infirmary where the margin and volume actually are. Alcohol-based: flammable, and in a dry campus keep it clearly shelved as a sanitiser, not near anything drinkable. 2-3 year shelf life but alcohol evaporates from poorly sealed cheap stock.

skuLines.line: Hearing aid amplifier and zinc-air button cells
skuLines.examples: Dr Trust 344 Hearing Aid Amplifier (live ₹1,680), Axon behind-the-ear amplifier, Siemens/Signia pocket aid; Rayovac / Power One zinc-air cells size 10/13/312/675
skuLines.priceBand: Amplifier ₹1,200-4,000 (fitted digital aids ₹8,000-60,000, order-in only); cells ₹80-300 per 6s
skuLines.seasonality: year-round
skuLines.notes: THE CELLS ARE THE REAL LINE, not the amplifier. Elderly residents who already own a fitted hearing aid need size 13/312/675 zinc-air cells every 1-2 weeks, and running out means they cannot hear for a week until someone goes to town. Stocking a ₹150 blister of cells solves a bigger problem than stocking the device. Zinc-air cells activate on tab removal and self-discharge — 2-3 year shelf life, buy fresh, rotate. Do not sell cheap amplifiers as substitutes for a proper audiologist fitting; there is no audiologist within 50 km, so be honest about the limits.

skuLines.examples: ready-made readers in +0.5 steps (Lenskart / local), Ojos readers, Vincent Chase readers, folding pocket readers
skuLines.packSizes: single, with case; power range +1.00 to +3.50 in +0.25/+0.50 steps
skuLines.seasonality: year-round
skuLines.marginBand: 40-60% — one of the best margins in the category
skuLines.notes: An easy line to overlook and a strong one for a closed township: presbyopia hits every staff member over 40, glasses get sat on and lost constantly, and the nearest optician is 30-50 km away. Carry a full power range with a small mirror and a test card at the counter. Not a substitute for an eye test — say so, and refer anyone with a real vision change to the campus hospital. Marginal on strict category definition (Class A device / accessory) but it belongs on this shelf here.

skuLines.line: Device batteries — AA, AAA, CR2032 and button cells
skuLines.examples: Duracell / Eveready AA and AAA, Panasonic CR2032, LR41 / LR44 / AG13 button cells, Maxell
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; spike Nov-Feb with device use
skuLines.notes: The most-missed line in every medical device shelf I would check. A thermometer, oximeter, BP monitor, weighing scale, nebuliser timer and glucometer are ALL dead without the right cell, and every one of them takes a different cell. If ARY sells the device and not the cell, the resident's device fails and they blame the store. Stock every cell type that any device on your shelf uses, and shelve them ON the device shelf as well as in electricals. Cheap, tiny, no cold chain, 5-10 year shelf life — there is no reason not to.

skuLines.line: Clinic-grade consumables for the campus infirmary and hospital
skuLines.examples: Romsons / Dispovan disposable syringes 2/5/10ml, needles, bulk sterile gauze rolls, Datt bulk cotton bandage, sharps container, IV/dressing consumables
skuLines.packSizes: boxes of 100 syringes; bulk gauze and cotton rolls; case packs
skuLines.priceBand: Syringe ₹8-18 each, box of 100 ₹120-400; bulk gauze roll ₹200-800; sharps bin ₹150-600
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; ordering peaks at academic-year start
skuLines.notes: Not a retail line — a B2B supply relationship with the school infirmary, the university health centre and the campus hospital, who are ordering these from somewhere already, probably from a distributor 50 km away. That is the largest single revenue opportunity in this category and the easiest to win on service (no freight, no minimum order, same-day). BUT: syringes, needles and several consumables are notified medical devices and sale requires the appropriate licence — settle the licence question with the HP Drug Controller before quoting. Do not duplicate the hospital's clinical role; be its stockroom.

trends2026: VERIFIED (IBEF): India's medical device market was US$15.35bn in 2023 heading to ~US$50bn by 2030 (16.4% CAGR), and domestic share of production has risen from 10% to 30% in five years, with 20% of advanced Class-C devices now made in India at 10-40% lower cost. Retail effect: far more credible Indian-made Class A/B devices (Dr Morepen, Dr Trust, AccuSure, Control D, BPL) at 30-40% below MNC pricing, with materially better retailer margin.

VERIFIED (IBEF): at-home diagnostics went mainstream in 2025 — Amazon Diagnostics launched in India in June 2025 with 800+ at-home lab tests across six cities. The habit of testing at home rather than travelling to a lab is exactly the behaviour a remote township adopts fastest, and it pulls device sales (BP, sugar, SpO2) along with it.

VERIFIED (IBEF): policy tailwinds are real — Rs 3,420 cr PLI for medical devices, National Medical Devices Policy 2023, medical device parks in UP, plus the India-UK FTA (Jul 2025, mutual recognition for Indian-certified devices) and the India-EU FTA (Jan 2026). Net effect at shelf level: more supply, more Indian brands, softer prices over the next 2-3 years.

INFERRED (not verified this session): Bluetooth/app-connected BP monitors and glucometers have become the default at the ₹2,500-4,000 tier (Omron Connect, Accu-Chek, Dr Trust, Beurer) — the premium device buyer now expects phone sync, and non-connected premium units are getting hard to sell.

INFERRED (not verified this session): continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) patches are moving from specialist to retail — Abbott FreeStyle Libre plus Indian programme players (BeatO, Sugarfit) at roughly ₹4,000-6,000 per 14-day sensor. At the premium end this starts to cannibalise test-strip volume, though for ARY's cohort strips remain the economic choice for years yet.

INFERRED (not verified this session): q-commerce (Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart) now delivers thermometers, oximeters, band-aids, crepe bandages and even nebulisers in 10-15 minutes in metros, which has reset what Indian consumers consider a reasonable wait. This is simultaneously the trend ARY cannot match and the gap it fills — q-commerce does not reach Rajgarh, so ARY IS the 10-minute store for 5,000 people.

INFERRED, VERIFY BEFORE ACTING: the September 2025 GST rationalisation is reported to have cut rates on many medical devices and consumables toward 5%, lowering shelf prices and changing margin arithmetic. Confirm current HSN-wise rates with ARY's own tax team before repricing anything.

INFERRED (not verified this session): post-COVID device ownership has normalised, so oximeters and nebulisers now sell on a REPLACEMENT cycle (2020-21 units failing) rather than on panic — steadier, more forecastable demand, and a reason to stock mid-tier rather than cheapest-possible units.

INFERRED (not verified this session): pharmacy and platform private labels (Tata 1mg, Apollo Life, Netmeds, Truemeds house brands) have taken real share in devices and dressings. The lesson for ARY is that a self-assembled ARY first aid kit and ARY-packed cotton/gauze capture 30-50% margin where branded equivalents give 8-15%.
adjacentServices: RENTAL of bulky mobility and recovery equipment — wheelchair, crutches, walker, commode chair, anti-bedsore air mattress, nebuliser — at ₹200-800/month against a refundable deposit. This is the highest-value service in the whole category for a township 30-50 km from a market: it converts stock that would sell twice a year into an asset that turns over 6-8 times, and it is a service residents genuinely cannot get anywhere else. Start with one wheelchair, one adult crutch pair, one child crutch pair, one walker.

Free health-check counter — BP, weight and SpO2 measured at the store by a trained staff member. In a captive township this makes ARY the de-facto screening point, and it is the classic Indian chemist hook: the reading creates the cuff sale, the strip sale and the follow-up visit.

Blood-sugar check at the counter using a store glucometer, charging ₹20-30 to recover the strip. Directly seeds the highest-annuity line in the category (test strips) and identifies, by name, the 30-60 diabetics whose brand and consumption you should be forecasting against.

Monthly refill subscription for glucose strips and lancets — a named list, a fixed reorder date, stock reserved. It kills both failure modes at once: the stock-out that forces a 100 km round trip, and the over-order that expires in monsoon humidity.

Warranty and service intake desk — take in a faulty BP monitor, nebuliser or weighing scale, courier it to the brand, return it to the resident. Nobody on this campus can make a 100 km round trip for a warranty claim, so this converts the biggest objection to buying a ₹2,000 device into a reason to buy it HERE rather than online.

Battery and consumable fitting bench — replace the LR44 in a thermometer, the CR2032 in a scale, the zinc-air cell in a hearing aid, fit a new BP cuff or nebuliser mask, replace a walking-stick ferrule. Two minutes of labour, sells a high-margin part, and it is the single most-appreciated service by elderly residents.

Institutional supply contract with a quarterly restock-and-expiry-check service for wall-mounted first aid boxes across every hostel wing, both canteens, the school, the university, labs, workshops, the warehouse and the school buses. Recurring, forecastable, and it is the largest revenue line in this category — the institutions are buying these from a distributor 50 km away today.

Dedicated kitchen burn kit programme for the two canteens — burn gel, non-adherent pads, cling film, cold packs — restocked on a schedule. A canteen scald is the predictable injury of a campus kitchen and nobody currently owns the restock.

Term-start hosteller first aid kit bundle, pre-packed and sold to parents at admission and at each term start (Apr and Jul). Captures margin on twelve SKUs in one ₹500 sale, at the one moment of the year when parents are willing to buy everything at once.

Expiry-reminder and swap service — keep a simple register of who bought strips, ORS, sterile dressings and kits, and tell them before it expires. In a closed community this costs almost nothing and prevents the most common quiet failure: a resident reaching for an expired kit in an emergency.

Referral discipline as a service, not a sale — a printed one-pager on when to stop self-treating and go to the campus hospital (low SpO2, a fever that will not break in a child, a wound that needs stitches). It protects residents, protects ARY, and makes the store the trusted first stop rather than a substitute for care.

HONESTY ON THE NUMBERS: every price band except the Dr Trust items above is a TYPICAL INDIAN RETAIL RANGE from prior domain knowledge of 2025-26 pricing, NOT scraped live this session. Margin bands are likewise indicative trade norms, not audited figures. Treat both as planning ranges to be confirmed against ARY's actual purchase invoices before they are used for buying or pricing decisions.

HONESTY ON THE REGULATION: the licence notes throughout (Medical Devices Rules 2017 risk classes A/B/C/D; retail sale of notified devices requiring a sale licence in Form MD-42 from the state licensing authority; OTC drugs such as ORS, Betadine ointment, Soframycin and Burnol requiring a separate retail drug licence in Form 20/21) are from prior knowledge — I could not fetch CDSCO or any regulatory explainer page this session. Confidence roughly 80%: the framework and the direction are right, but the exact form numbers, the current notified-device list and the compliance dates MUST be confirmed with the Himachal Pradesh Drug Controller before ARY lists devices or clinic consumables. Do not act on my form numbers alone.

POPULATION REASONING, not a source: the cohort, essentiality, seasonality and hill-logistics judgements are derived from the brief's own facts (5,000 residents; children 5-18 in residential school; 18-25 university; married staff with babies; elderly; PIN 173101 cold hill with heavy monsoon; nearest market 30-50 km; two canteens; no tobacco or alcohol) applied to standard Indian retail assortment practice. They are inference, clearly marked as such, and were NOT checked against what ARY actually stocks — the brief required this stage to stay blind to ARY's own catalogue, and no ary CLI command was run.
